source.title: Parvalbumin+ interneurons obey unique connectivity rules and establish a powerful lateral-inhibition microcircuit in dentate gyrus

confidence_rationale: This is the single strongest biological reference for the SD-016 H3 (hard/competitive selection) leg, and it is unusually direct: it does not merely assert that the dentate gyrus performs winner-take-all selection, it measures the connectivity statistics that would be REQUIRED for a WTA circuit and shows the dentate gyrus has them while neocortex does not. 9098 tested connections across 270 slices via up to octuple simultaneous patch-clamp is exceptional methodological quality for a connectivity study. Mapping fidelity is high but not maximal: the paper establishes that the ARCHITECTURE affords WTA, not that WTA selection is observed in behaving animals, so the REE translation ('build the competitive operator into the circuit rather than hoping a downstream loss induces it') is licensed structurally rather than functionally. Transfer risk moderate-low: the finding is an architectural/statistical property of a microcircuit, which is the level REE is actually importing from, so the usual rodent-to-artificial-agent worry bites less than it would for a behavioural result. Weighted toward mapping_fidelity per the skill's guidance for architectural claims.
failure_signatures: Lateral inhibition dominance is a property of the DENTATE GYRUS specifically -- in neocortex, entorhinal cortex and presubiculum, recurrent inhibition is equally or more abundant than lateral inhibition, which the authors state 'would seem incompatible with efficient pattern separation'. So competitive selection is not a generic property of cortical circuits that REE can assume; it is a specialisation that must be deliberately built.

Recurrent inhibition (a unit inhibiting itself) is argued to be actively COUNTER-PRODUCTIVE for WTA because it suppresses potential winners. A naive REE implementation that applies an undifferentiated inhibition/normalisation term across all slots (including self-inhibition) may reproduce the failure mode rather than the fix.

Unitary GC->PV EPSPs (mean 1.79 mV) were measured in vivo to be insufficient to trigger a spike alone against a 10.3 mV threshold gap -- the competitive mechanism depends on SPATIAL SUMMATION across many converging units, so a competitive operator over too few slots (or with too weak convergence) may not engage at all.

Reciprocal GC-PV motifs were NOT significantly enriched, contrary to the neocortical prior the authors tested against. An REE design that imports 'the standard cortical E-I motif' would import the wrong statistics.
The recordings are in vitro slice at ~22 C in juvenile mice (P20-44); connection probabilities may differ in adult, awake, behaving conditions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In the dentate gyrus, lateral inhibition (a granule cell inhibiting NEIGHBOURING granule cells via a PV+ interneuron) is ~10-times more abundant than recurrent inhibition (a granule cell inhibiting itself) -- a ratio of 9.25 (296 unidirectional vs 32 bidirectional connections in 1301 tested GC-PV pairs). Excitatory GC->PV connectivity is focal (peak 11.3%, space constant 144 um) while inhibitory PV->GC connectivity is broader and stronger (peak 28.9%, space constant 215 um), giving an inhibition:excitation connection-probability ratio of 3.83. The authors conclude these unique connectivity rules are 'well suited' to a winner-takes-all mechanism: 'a small population of activated winner cells must be able to efficiently and rapidly inhibit a large population of non-winner cells'.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-016's cue->slot tagger selects one of 16 ContextMemory slots given z_world. The biological analogue of that selection is the DG granule-cell population choosing which sparse subset fires given entorhinal input. This paper says the mechanism that accomplishes it is STRUCTURAL -- an asymmetric, spatially-organised lateral-inhibition motif wired into the circuit -- and NOT a differentiable objective that happens to reward sparsity downstream. This directly supports the GOV-FANOUT-1 H3 leg's premise: the fix for the uniform-softmax saddle (sel_entropy pinned at ln(16)=2.7726 across three independently-designed mechanisms) is to change the SELECTION OPERATOR to a hard/competitive one (k-winner-take-all with cross-slot inhibition), rather than to add another auxiliary loss on top of a plain softmax. The specific design guidance it supplies is sharper than 'add competition': make inhibition LATERAL (slot i suppresses slots j != i) and NOT recurrent (slot i must not suppress itself), make the suppressive reach BROADER than the excitatory drive (the 3.83 ratio and the 215 vs 144 um space constants), and note that the winner is decided by relative drive against a shared inhibitory pool rather than by an absolute threshold per slot.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures ANATOMICAL/functional connectivity statistics and argues from them that the circuit AFFORDS winner-take-all -- it does not demonstrate WTA dynamics during behaviour, and the authors are explicit that whether pattern separation and gamma oscillation generation can coexist in this circuit 'remains to be determined'. So this licenses the SHAPE of an REE competitive operator, not a quantitative parameterisation. Two further gaps: (i) the DG's competition is over ~1e6 granule cells at ~5% activation, whereas SD-016 selects over 16 slots -- the ratio of winners to competitors differs by orders of magnitude, and a k-WTA over 16 slots may be closer to a hard argmax than to biological sparse coding, which is a genuine scale disanalogy and NOT one this paper can adjudicate; (ii) the spatial organisation (space constants in micrometres) has no counterpart in an REE slot array with no metric topology, so the 'lateral' structure must be imported as all-to-all-minus-self inhibition rather than as distance-graded inhibition, which is a real simplification of what was measured.
mapping.source_context: In vitro hippocampal slice, genetically-labelled PV/SST/CCK interneurons in mouse (P20-44, both sexes), simultaneous whole-cell patch-clamp of up to 8 neurons; supplemented by 3 in vivo whole-cell recordings from fast-spiking DG interneurons in awake head-fixed mice on a treadmill.

confidence_components.notes: Nature Communications, Peter Jonas lab (the reference lab for hippocampal microcircuit electrophysiology). 9098 tested connections, bootstrap-controlled motif analysis against a distance-matched random network with Benjamini-Hochberg correction -- the statistical design directly addresses the 'is this just chance connectivity' objection. Mapping fidelity 0.80 rather than higher because the WTA interpretation is the authors' inference from connectivity statistics, not a measured dynamic. Transfer risk 0.30 reflects the 16-slot vs 1e6-granule-cell scale disanalogy and the absence of a spatial metric in the REE slot array, partly offset by the fact that REE is importing an architectural motif (the level at which this paper is strongest) rather than a behavioural effect size.
